tar_spot.description: Fungal foliar disease causing small, raised, black circular to oval structures (stromata) on leaf blades, leaf sheaths, and husks. Can lead to rapid blight, premature dry-down, and severe stalk lodging.
tar_spot.treatment: Apply a dual- or triple-mode of action fungicide containing QoI (strobilurin, Group 11), DMI (triazole, Group 3), and/or SDHI (Group 7) active ingredients. Multiple university trials demonstrate optimal economic response when applied between VT (tasseling) and R3 (milk stage). If weather remains cool (60–72°F) and humid with prolonged leaf wetness (>7 hours daily), a second application may be required.
tar_spot.active_ingredients: Mefentrifluconazole + Pyraclostrobin + Fluxapyroxad (Group 3 + 11 + 7, e.g., Revytek) or Prothioconazole + Trifloxystrobin + Fluopyram (Delaro Complete)
tar_spot.rate: 8.0 fl oz/acre (Revytek) or 8.0 to 10.0 fl oz/acre (Delaro Complete)
tar_spot.interval: 14 to 21 days between applications if environmental conditions favor continued disease spread
tar_spot.preharvest_interval: Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI): 30 days for field corn grain and stover; 14 days for sweet corn or silage
tar_spot.economic_threshold: Presence of active stromata on leaves at or below the ear leaf prior to R3 stage with cool, humid weather forecast (>75% RH).
tar_spot.safety_notes: EPA Signal Word: CAUTION. Personal Protective Equipment (PPE): Chemical-resistant gloves (Barrier Laminate, Butyl Rubber ≥14 mils), long-sleeved shirt, long pants, protective eyewear, shoes plus socks. High aquatic toxicity; maintain mandatory 25-foot untreated vegetative buffer adjacent to surface waters.
tar_spot.source_title: Crop Protection Network (CPN-2012) & Iowa State University Extension and Outreach Publication IPM 0044: Fungicide Efficacy for Control of Corn Diseases

gray_leaf_spot.description: Fungal pathogen producing distinct rectangular, vein-delimited necrotic lesions (tan to gray) that run parallel with leaf veins. Spreads upward from lower canopy residue during extended warm, humid periods.
gray_leaf_spot.treatment: Fungicide application recommended at VT (tasseling) to R1 (silking) if lesions are observed on the third leaf below the ear leaf on 50% or more of plants in susceptible or moderately susceptible hybrids. Implement crop rotation with non-hosts (soybeans) and reduce surface residue where permissible.
gray_leaf_spot.active_ingredients: Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole (Group 11 + 3, e.g., Quadris Top SBX) or Pyraclostrobin + Fluxapyroxad (Priaxor)
gray_leaf_spot.rate: 10.0 to 14.4 fl oz/acre (Quadris Top SBX) or 4.0 to 8.0 fl oz/acre (Priaxor)
gray_leaf_spot.interval: 14 to 21 days if high humidity and canopy dew persist
gray_leaf_spot.preharvest_interval: Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI): 30 days before harvest for grain or silage
gray_leaf_spot.economic_threshold: Lesions present on the third leaf below the ear leaf on 50% of plants at VT-R1 in susceptible hybrids under humid conditions (>85% RH).
gray_leaf_spot.safety_notes: EPA Signal Word: WARNING (Causes substantial but temporary eye injury). Mandatory protective eyewear, chemical-resistant gloves, coveralls over short-sleeved shirt and short pants. Wash thoroughly with soap and water after handling.
gray_leaf_spot.source_title: Purdue University Extension Publication BP-89-W: Corn Disease Management - Gray Leaf Spot & CPN-2015

northern_corn_leaf_blight.description: Fungal foliar disease causing characteristic cigar-shaped, elliptical grayish-green to tan lesions (1 to 6 inches long). Severe early blighting destroys functional green leaf area, causing substantial grain fill reduction.
northern_corn_leaf_blight.treatment: Apply multi-mode fungicide prior to silking (VT to R1) if lesions develop on leaves below the ear leaf on 50% or more of plants and weather is moderate (65–80°F) with frequent dews. Select corn hybrids with qualitative Ht single-gene resistance or multi-genic quantitative resistance for subsequent crop cycles.
northern_corn_leaf_blight.active_ingredients: Propiconazole + Azoxystrobin (Group 3 + 11, e.g., Quilt Xcel) or Pyraclostrobin (Headline AMP)
northern_corn_leaf_blight.rate: 10.5 to 14.0 fl oz/acre (Quilt Xcel) or 10.0 to 14.4 fl oz/acre (Headline AMP)
northern_corn_leaf_blight.interval: 14 to 21 days if conducive cool, wet microclimate continues
northern_corn_leaf_blight.preharvest_interval: Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI): 30 days for grain; 14 days for forage/silage
northern_corn_leaf_blight.economic_threshold: Lesions present on 50% of leaves below the ear leaf prior to silking (VT-R1) in susceptible varieties.
northern_corn_leaf_blight.safety_notes: EPA Signal Word: CAUTION. Protective gloves, long sleeves, eye protection required. Avoid spray drift to non-target crops and bodies of water.
northern_corn_leaf_blight.source_title: University of Illinois Extension Field Crop Disease Guide & Crop Protection Network (CPN-2015)

common_rust.description: Airborne obligate parasite forming cinnamon-brown, powdery oval to elongate pustules (uredinia) scattered on both the upper and lower leaf surfaces. Pustules rupture the epidermis, releasing brownish spores.
common_rust.treatment: Fungicide treatment in commercial dent corn is rarely economically justified because modern field corn hybrids have strong adult-plant resistance (Rp genes). Treatment is only warranted on high-value seed corn inbreds or sweet corn if pustule coverage exceeds 10% of ear leaf area prior to blister stage (R2).
common_rust.rate: 6.0 to 9.0 fl oz/acre (Headline) or 10.5 fl oz/acre (Quilt Xcel)
common_rust.interval: Single targeted application usually sufficient; re-evaluate after 14 days only on high-value seed production fields
common_rust.preharvest_interval: Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI): 7 days for field corn; 0 days for sweet corn fresh market
common_rust.economic_threshold: Pustules covering >10% of leaf area on or above ear leaf before R2 stage on susceptible seed corn lines.
common_rust.safety_notes: EPA Signal Word: CAUTION. Standard agricultural worker safety standards apply. Toxic to freshwater fish and invertebrates.
common_rust.source_title: Iowa State University Extension and Outreach: Corn Rust Identification and Management (Publication PM 1785)

healthy.description: Intact green leaf blade with normal parallel venation, healthy chlorophyll coloration, and absence of fungal stromata, blighted lesions, or rust pustules.
healthy.treatment: No chemical fungicide treatment recommended. Continue standard Integrated Pest Management (IPM) scouting on a weekly schedule through R4 (dough) stage. Maintain balanced nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium soil fertility. Preserving natural beneficial epiphytic microbes avoids unnecessary chemical expenditure.
healthy.safety_notes: No chemical hazards. Follow standard field safety precautions against heat and equipment.
healthy.source_title: USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS) & Iowa State University Integrated Pest Management Scouting Guide

unsure.description: Visual features are insufficient or ambiguous to produce a confident diagnosis. Possible causes: non-leaf subject, severe lens blur, harsh direct sunlight/shadow glare, insect frass mimicking tar spot stromata, or early uncharacteristic chlorotic flecking.
unsure.treatment:
DO NOT apply chemical treatments based on an unconfirmed scan. Immediate field troubleshooting steps:
1. Physical Water Rub Test: Moisten a cloth or thumb and firmly wipe 5 suspicious spots. If spots rub off onto the rag, it is insect frass (bug feces), NOT fungal tar spot.
2. Retake Scouting Photograph: Hold phone camera 6 to 8 inches from leaf blade, ensure leaf is in sharp focus, avoid direct midday glare by shading the leaf with your body, and include both green tissue and lesion border.
3. Physical Diagnostic Clinic Submission: If foliar symptoms spread over 48 hours, place 3 whole symptomatic leaves between dry paper towels in a plastic bag and mail to your State Land-Grant University Plant Diagnostic Clinic.
unsure.active_ingredients: None (Chemical application withheld pending verified diagnosis)
unsure.economic_threshold: Do not treat without confirmed threshold.
unsure.safety_notes: Do not apply agricultural chemicals without positive pest/disease identification.
unsure.source_title: Iowa State University Plant and Insect Diagnostic Clinic (PIDC) Sample Submission Protocol & Purdue Plant and Pest Diagnostic Laboratory (PPDL)
